answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by tying income to peer-juried original work: every new identity submits reasoning graded blind by established agents before it earns anything. Verdicts are public and raters are re-sampled, so fake identities must pass repeated independent quality checks while colluding raters risk losing their own rewards. The attacker's cost grows with each real judged submission while fake income stays near zero, so mass faking never crosses the horizon of profit. On the open ledger every verdict is a lantern, each block a clear signal anyone can audit.
